Policy Learning for Social Robot-Led Physiotherapy
Carl Bettosi1,2, Lynne Baillie1, Susan Shenkin3 and Marta Romeo1
Abstract— Social robots offer a promising solution for au-
tonomously guiding patients through physiotherapy exercise
sessions, but effective deployment requires advanced decision-
making to adapt to patient needs. A key challenge is the scarcity
of patient behavior data for developing robust policies. To
address this, we engaged 33 expert healthcare practitioners
as patient proxies, using their interactions with our robot
to inform a patient behavior model capable of generating
exercise performance metrics and subjective scores on perceived
exertion. We trained a reinforcement learning-based policy in
simulation, demonstrating that it can adapt exercise instructions
to individual exertion tolerances and fluctuating performance,
while also being applicable to patients at different recovery
stages with varying exercise plans.
I. INTRODUCTION
Adherence to physical exercise programs is crucial for
rehabilitating individuals who have sustained injuries such
as fractures or strokes, significantly improving physical out-
comes while delivering broader social and economic bene-
fits [1]. However, healthcare workforce shortages in many
countries mean patients can go weeks or months without in-
person physiotherapy assessments, meaning they often rely
on generic paper or video-based exercise guides [2]. While
